name: empty-on-failure
description: `if (!res.ok) return []` collapses two answers that mean opposite things: 'you have none' and 'we could not look'. The second, rendered as the first, states a fact about the customer's own data out of a failure to read it — and this repo has already paid for it, showing a customer with two hundred parcels the NEW-USER ONBOARDING STATE during an API blip and inviting them to add their first parcels (see client/src/lib/fetch-honesty.ts). The helpers to say which you mean have existed since that fix: `okOrThrow` for anything answering 'what do I have', `nullOn404` for an OPTIONAL single record where 404 is a real answer and every other status is still a failure. Four files adopted them. This ratchet counts what has not, and drives it DOWN — lower baselineCount whenever a call site converts.
lastBumpNote: 7 -> 5 on 2026-09-05: the two chat reads, converted — the last entries on the triage's CONVERT list, and the only two that were ever blocked rather than deliberately kept. use-founder-chat.ts (a thread's message history) and use-founder-chat-threads.ts (the thread list) now use okOrThrow, and both catch blocks are gone. What unblocked them is the part the prior note said had to come first: A PLACE TO RENDER THE FAILURE. useFounderChat now returns historyUnavailable / retryHistory / historyRetrying alongside its status machine, and the failure surface is one shared component — client/src/components/founder-chat/ChatUnavailable.tsx — rendered by ALL THREE chat surfaces that read these two queries: founder-chat/Dock.tsx, founder-bridge/BridgeAtlasPane.tsx and founder-bridge/BridgeAtlasSheet.tsx. Three, not one, because the throw lands in every consumer of the hook and a failure message that lives in only the Dock is a lie in the other two — the second law's adoption half, applied to a component. Two adjacent empty-state lies went with them, both reachable only on a failed read: the pane's thread-count badge rendered the count 0, and the sheet's peek summary greeted the founder with 'Morning, Tom. Tap to start a thread.' — a fresh-account greeting shown to someone whose threads simply could not be read. THE FIVE THAT REMAIN ARE THE TRIAGE'S 'KEEP' LIST, ENTIRE: use-ui-state, use-list-view, theme-context and use-sovereign-dashboard's notification preferences are PREFERENCE syncs whose design is 'server unavailable, keep what is local', and version-check polls /api/version for a newer build. None is a claim about the customer's own data. Converting them would drive this number to 0 and make the product worse. THIS RATCHET IS THEREFORE AT ITS FLOOR: a future drop is evidence of a mistake, not progress, and 5 should only fall if one of those five stops being a preference read. PRIOR NOTE — 14 -> 7 on 2026-09-05: the whole nullOn404 group from the triage, converted. Each was an OPTIONAL SINGLE RECORD where a 404 is a real answer and every other status was rendering identically to it — land-credit-badge (a scored property looked unscored whenever the read failed), maps' AVM valuation, research-summary comps, founder money's unit economics and paid-data readiness, and the autonomy score and revenue attribution in use-sovereign-dashboard. `nullOn404` keeps the 404 and throws the rest. Two inner `catch { return null }` blocks went with them: a body that will not parse is not an absent measurement either. THE SEVEN THAT REMAIN ARE THE TRIAGE'S OWN 'KEEP' LIST PLUS THE TWO CHAT CONVERSIONS: use-ui-state, use-list-view, theme-context and the notification preferences in use-sovereign-dashboard are PREFERENCE syncs designed to fall back to local state; version-check polls /api/version for a newer build; and use-founder-chat / use-founder-chat-threads still need a place to render a failure before their throw is safe to add (useFounderChat carries its own idle/streaming status machine, and Dock.tsx picks threads[0] with no branch for 'there was no list'). Converting the five preference reads would drive this number to 2 and make the product worse, which is the reason the triage is in the note and not just the count. PRIOR NOTE — 15 -> 14 on 2026-09-04: use-sovereign-dashboard.ts:18 (useAgentRuntimeStates) converted to okOrThrow, WITH the error branch its consumer needed. agent-performance.tsx rendered a failed read as "No agent data available yet. Agents will appear once the system initializes." — a claim about the fleet's state that a failed read has no business making. The non-array body case now throws too, for the same reason: a shape the hook does not recognise is a contract failure, not an idle fleet. The two remaining okOrThrow candidates (use-founder-chat.ts:94 and use-founder-chat-threads.ts:50) are NOT done here and are not half-done either: the chat dock has no place to render a failure today — useFounderChat carries its own idle/streaming status machine that would need a 'history unavailable' state — and shipping the throw without it would trade a wrong sentence for a silently dead dock. PRIOR NOTE — Created at 15 on 2026-09-04, measured. THE BASELINE IS PRE-EXISTING DEBT THIS GATE NEVER COVERED, not approval: fetch-honesty.ts was written in an earlier fix, documented the defect and shipped the helpers, and then nothing counted the sites that had not converted — authoritative semantics with no drift prevention, which CLAUDE.md names as one third of what 'canonical' requires. The commit that created this fixed the SYSTEMIC half separately: `fetchJsonArray` in client/src/lib/queryClient.ts (47 call sites across 15 files) returned [] on a 500, on an unparseable body and on an unrecognised shape, and now throws RequestFailedError — so the react-query call lands in its error state and the page renders QueryErrorState with a retry. Four components that had no error branch gained one, because a throw with nothing rendering it is the same empty state by another route: pipeline-velocity ('No active deals to analyze. Add deals to see pipeline velocity.'), QuickAddSheet's notes and properties forms ('No notes to log against', 'No properties yet'), and team-chat-panel, whose messages query was a bare `fetch(...).then(r => r.json())` with NO res.ok check at all — a 500 body parsed fine, messages defaulted to [], and the panel said 'No messages yet. Start the conversation!' about a thread the team had been using for months. THE PATTERN'S OWN BUG, recorded because it is the class this repo pays for most: the first draft ended the alternation with `\b`, which after `[]` can never match — `]` and `;` are both non-word characters, so there is no boundary between them. That silently excluded every `return []` and `return {}`, the two commonest spellings, and measured 12 instead of 15. Found by cross-checking the regex against an independent grep rather than trusting its own number. THE 15 ARE TRIAGED, so the next reader converts rather than re-reads. The discriminator is WHAT THE VALUE IS A CLAIM ABOUT: a PREFERENCE that falls back to local state is not a claim about the customer's data and is correct as it stands; a DATA read that renders as 'you have none' is the defect. KEEP (5) — use-ui-state.ts:59 and use-list-view.ts:71 and theme-context.tsx:140 are preference syncs whose whole design is 'server unavailable, keep what is local'; use-sovereign-dashboard.ts:233 is notification preferences, the same shape; and version-check.ts:53 polls /api/version to ask whether a newer build exists — a failed poll is not customer data and must not throw a UI into an error state. Converting these would make the gate look better and the product worse. CONVERT TO okOrThrow (3) — the LIST reads, where [] renders as a factual claim: use-founder-chat.ts:94 ('this thread is empty'), use-founder-chat-threads.ts:50 ('you have no conversations') and use-sovereign-dashboard.ts:18 ('no agents running'). Each needs an error branch at its consumer first — agent-performance.tsx and founder-chat/Dock.tsx have none — because a throw with nothing rendering it is the same empty state by another route, which is the lesson the fetchJsonArray half of this commit already paid for. CONVERT TO nullOn404 (7) — optional single records where 404 is a real answer and every other status is not: land-credit-badge.tsx:106, maps.tsx:485 (AVM valuation), research-summary-panel.tsx:166 (comps), money.tsx:416 (unit economics), money.tsx:853 (paid data readiness), use-sovereign-dashboard.ts:50 (autonomy score) and :107 (revenue attribution). These render 'unavailable' rather than 'you have none', so the harm is smaller and the conversion is defence in depth rather than a live fix — do them, but after the three above.
minimaNote: VACUITY FLOOR on the SCAN POPULATION, not a ratchet. baselineCount counts BAD THINGS FOUND, so a walk that stops seeing client files finds zero and reports it as progress. MEASURED 2026-09-04: these globs matched 868 files. Floor set to 700, comfortably below, so a broken glob trips it while ordinary deletion does not. If a real deletion wave takes the population under this floor, lower the floor in the same commit and name the wave — never raise it to silence something, never delete the key.
